On The 6 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 5473 of 2022
 Smt. Maya And Others
 Versus
 Narayan Gujar And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Chandra Prakash Purohit, learned counsel for t
 Ms. Bhagyashree Gupta, learned counsel for the resp
 Order
The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 31.03.2022 passed in claim case No.2661/2019.
2. The factum of accident and liability of insurance company is not under dispute.

3. The short facts of the case are that on 01.12.2019 the husband of the appellant No.1-Mahesh Patidar was going by his motorcycle bearing registration number MP09-ND-7136 from Mhow to Gavli Palasiya and when he reached near Bherulal Patidar College, in front of shop of Ishwar Seth,
Car No.MP09-CN-9965 was coming from the side of Manpur which was being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of the deceased- Mahesh from the front.
This accident resulted in the cascading accident with another motorcycle No.MP09-MD-6072.
The 2 MA-5473-2022 deceased Mahesh was admitted in Choithram Hospital, Indore where he died during treatment on 02.02.2019.
The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for the compensation of death of Mahesh in the above said accident.
The claims tribunal considering the evidence on record awarded a total sum of Rs.10,89,000/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income of the deceased has been assessed on notional basis at Rs.10,000/- per month.

He by referring to Ex.P-17 to Ex.P-20 submits that the income tax returns for the year 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18 and 2018-19 were submitted in which the income of the deceased was shown as Rs.5,71,724/-, Rs.5,71,721/- Rs.5,79,850/- and Rs.5,71,576/-.
He thus submits that in view of the income tax returns the conclusion of the claims tribunal in assessing income of the appellant at Rs.10,000/- on notional basis is not correct.
His income should have been taken in accordance with the income tax returns submitted by the appellants.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent submits that the claims tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the appellant as Rs.10,000/- per month for the fact that on perusal of income tax returns it would come to the fore that the income of the deceased was from agricultural land,

1 house rent and business.
She submits that only an amount of Rs.1,85,816/- was shown to be accruing from business and thus, the rest of the amount was from house rent and agricultural land.
She, thus, submits that even after the death of Mahesh this income would continue to come.

Thus,
the entire amount as mentioned in the income tax returns cannot be taken for consideration for 3 MA-5473-2022 assessing the income of the deceased.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
It is seen from the record of the case that indeed the income tax returns were there in which aforesaid amount was mentioned as income of the deceased.
To some extent it is also correct that the part of the income as mentioned in the above said document would continue to come.
Thus, the loss of dependency has to be assessed by balancing the aforesaid fact.
In the fitness of things, this Court deems it fit to award a lump-sum amount of Rs.2,50,000/-.
This amount shall be over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% from the date of application presented before the claims tribunal.
8. In view of the above, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
